blocks.text: How Square-Foot Volume Compresses Renovation Dust Remediation Unit Rates

In commercial janitorial procurement, unit pricing per square foot never scales linearly across facility sizes. Just as routine ongoing office cleaning drops from $0.12–$0.20 per square foot in suites under 2,500 square feet down to $0.05–$0.10 per square foot in facilities exceeding 25,000 square feet, specialty tenant improvement (TI) renovation dust cleanup exhibits a steep volume curve.

When a small 1,800-square-foot dental admin suite or boutique wealth-management office undergoes a drywall and flooring refresh, the janitorial contractor still incurs two hours of non-billable van loading, chemical mixing, HEPA filter preparation, travel time, and loading-dock check-in. Spread across 1,800 square feet, that fixed setup cost adds $0.09 to $0.14 per square foot before a single window sill is wiped. Across a 30,000-square-foot regional headquarters build-out, the exact same mobilization overhead adds less than $0.01 per square foot, and multi-person crews establish specialized assembly-line task roles.

blocks.text: Why Small Office Suites (Under 2,500 Sq Ft) Face Premium Per-Sq-Ft Rates

Facility managers overseeing a 1,500- to 2,400-square-foot suite renovation are frequently surprised when quotes come back at $0.30 to $0.45 per square foot—or as a flat $450 to $850 project fee. Three structural realities drive small-suite unit premiums:

items: High Perimeter-to-Floor-Area Ratio: Small suites consist mostly of private perimeter offices, a reception lobby, a kitchenette, and one or two restrooms. Detail cleaning interior door frames, window mullions, baseboards, and cabinet interiors takes 3x longer per square foot than cleaning open-plan bullpen space.

Minimum Crew Dispatch & Specialty Hourly Floor: Because OSHA safety practices and ladder spotting require at least a two-person team for post-renovation high dusting, a 4-hour minimum shift for two specialty technicians (8 labor hours at $55 to $95 per hour) establishes a hard labor floor of $440 to $760 regardless of how small the suite is.
Manual Tool Constraint: Tight hallways and furnished private offices prevent the use of walk-behind auto-scrubbers. Technicians must hand-vacuum and damp-mop every square foot manually.

blocks.title: How Small Offices Can Trim 20% Off Renovation Cleanup Bids
blocks.text: If your office is under 2,500 square feet and located inside a multi-tenant commercial building, ask the building's incumbent base-building janitorial contractor to quote the TI dust cleanup. Because their equipment, supervisory staff, and insurance COI are already staged on site every evening, they can waive the $185 to $350 truck mobilization fee and schedule two technicians immediately after their normal shift.
How Large Floors (10,000 to 25,000+ Sq Ft) Unlock Production Efficiencies

Once a tenant improvement project crosses the 10,000-square-foot threshold—and especially in 25,000+ square foot multi-floor corporate build-outs—janitorial estimators shift from generalist two-person teams to division-of-labor production crews. Instead of every worker switching back and forth between extension wands, backpack vacuums, razor scrapers, and mop buckets, a 6- to 10-person project crew operates in synchronized waves:

items.name: Wave 1: High-Reach Plenum & Diffuser Extraction
items.text: Two technicians equipped with backpack HEPA vacuums and 16-foot extension poles move continuously ahead of the crew, clearing HVAC supply vents, light troughs, and door headers so all dislodged dust falls to the uncleaned floor.

items.name: Wave 2: Vertical Glass, Millwork & Partition Detailing
items.text: A dedicated glass and millwork specialist scrapes paint and silicone off conference partitions and damp-wipes cabinetry, switch plates, and window sills from shoulder height down to the baseboard.

items.name: Wave 3: Restroom & Wet-Core Deep Sanitization
items.text: A restroom specialist descales ceramic tile and grout (1.12x flooring multiplier), polishes chrome flush valves, and disinfects all high-touch surfaces without holding up the main floor crew.

items.name: Wave 4: Wide-Area HEPA Floor Extraction & Multi-Pass Wet Rinse
items.text: Floor technicians sweep through open corridors and workstation zones using 24- to 28-inch wide-area HEPA vacuums or cylindrical auto-scrubbers, achieving 1,400 to 1,800 square feet per labor hour.

blocks.text: Equipment Selection Across Small-Suite vs. Large-Floor Turnovers

Even on large floor plates where ride-on or walk-behind scrubbers handle main corridors, corners, restroom cores, breakrooms, and threshold transitions require commercial manual wet-mopping and EPA-registered surface disinfection to eliminate lingering drywall film and construction contaminants. Specifying high-capacity, low-linting wet tools prevents streaks and minimizes bucket refill trips across expansive buildings.

For heavy post-renovation hard-floor rinsing where drywall slurry must be lifted cleanly from VCT, LVT, or ceramic tile joints, crews pair the Rubbermaid Commercial Super Stitch Blend Mop Head 24-oz (engineered with a balanced 24 oz Cotton/Synth yarn blend and looped ends for Launderable durability and Medium Duty floor release) with the Alpine Commercial 36-Quart Side-Press Mop Bucket (featuring a generous 36 qt basin that keeps rinse water cleaner longer, a high-leverage Side-Press wringer, non-marking 3-in Casters, and an integrated Pour Spout for fast slop-sink draining). Once all construction dust has been physically extracted and rinsed from breakrooms, restrooms, and executive suites, technicians apply the Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray 19-oz Case (12-Pack) (packaged in 12 x 19 oz commercial cans with an EPA Reg formula that Kills 99.9% of bacteria and viruses and leaves a clean Crisp Linen finish) across door hardware, conference room push plates, and restroom fixtures prior to tenant handover.
Fixture Density vs. Open Bullpen Ratios: The Hidden Volume Modifier

When comparing two quotes of equal square footage, always inspect the architectural density ratio. A 15,000-square-foot call center or tech engineering floor featuring 80% open carpet tile and two multi-stall core restrooms will price near the bottom of the bracket ($0.15 to $0.18 per square foot). Conversely, a 15,000-square-foot law firm or medical-adjacent corporate suite packed with 45 glass-front partner offices, three coffee pantries, wood veneer wainscoting (1.08x hardwood/wood care multiplier), and six private single-user restrooms behaves like seven small offices stitched together—pushing the unit price toward $0.24 to $0.28 per square foot.

blocks.title: Connecting TI Volume Tiers to Post-Occupancy Monthly Retainers
blocks.text: When soliciting bids for a 10,000+ square foot renovation cleanup, bundle your request for proposal (RFP) with the subsequent 12-month recurring janitorial contract. Vendors competing for an ongoing 5x-week daily weekday contract (21.65 visits/month at a 0.90 frequency multiplier and $0.07 to $0.12/sq ft) routinely discount the one-time TI dust remediation rate by 15% to 25% to win the long-term monthly account.

faqs.q: Why does a 2,000-square-foot office renovation cleanup cost almost half as much as a 6,000-square-foot cleanup?
faqs.a: Small jobs under 2,500 square feet are governed by minimum dispatch economics and high fixture density. Dispatching a two-person specialty crew with commercial HEPA vacuums, wet scrubbers, and step ladders requires a minimum 4-hour labor block plus truck mobilization ($450 to $850 minimum). Once the crew is on site with equipment set up, expanding the scope from 2,000 to 6,000 square feet of open carpet only adds incremental vacuuming and mopping hours without doubling fixed overhead.

faqs.q: At what square footage do contractors switch from per-visit flat fees to per-square-foot unit pricing?
faqs.a: Most commercial janitorial estimators switch from flat minimum project pricing to strict per-square-foot calculation right around 2,500 to 3,500 square feet. Below 2,500 square feet, the labor time required to clean the restroom, breakroom, and entry glass dominates the bid; above 3,500 square feet, open floor and corridor square footage becomes the primary driver of total crew hours.

faqs.q: How do large multi-floor renovations structure phased turnover billing?
faqs.a: On 25,000+ square foot projects where floors are handed over in separate 10,000-square-foot phases spaced weeks apart, contractors typically price the total square footage at the 10,000–24,999 sq ft tier ($0.15 to $0.25/sq ft) rather than the 25,000+ sq ft single-mobilization tier ($0.11 to $0.21/sq ft), because each separate phase requires its own truck mobilization, freight elevator reservation, and supervisor sign-off.

faqs.q: Does building size affect Certificate of Insurance (COI) requirements for renovation cleanup?
faqs.a: Yes. While a small suburban office park suite under 2,500 square feet typically requires a standard $1 million per occurrence / $2 million aggregate General Liability COI, large Class A towers housing 25,000+ square foot tenants routinely mandate $5 million to $10 million in umbrella excess liability coverage, completed-operations endorsements, and strict union or prevailing-wage compliance.
